title: വേഴാമ്പൽ ജീവിതം Hornbills: Forest Royals with Sealed Secrets #Bird facts #malayalam
description:
Kerala is home to some of the most iconic and mysterious birds in India — the hornbills. With their massive curved beaks, helmet-like casques, and loud wingbeats, these birds are the guardians of the forest canopy.

In this video, explore the 4 species of hornbills found in Kerala:

🟡 1. Great Indian Hornbill (Buceros bicornis)
The largest hornbill in India, also known as "Malabar Vezhambal".

Males have a large yellow casque and black-white body with a stunning golden beak.

They are symbols of love and fidelity, as they mate for life.

Found in the Periyar Tiger Reserve, Silent Valley, and Agasthyarkoodam forests.

🟢 2. Malabar Grey Hornbill (Ocyceros griseus)
Endemic to the Western Ghats.

Smaller and entirely grey, without a prominent casque.

Found near human habitats, plantations, and evergreen forests.

Plays a major role in seed dispersal in lowland forests.

🔵 3. Indian Grey Hornbill (Ocyceros birostris)
Found mostly in dry deciduous forests of the Palakkad and Wayanad regions.

Has a prominent dark grey casque and lighter body color.

Commonly spotted near villages and open woodlands.

🔴 4. Malabar Pied Hornbill (Anthracoceros coronatus)
A rare and near-threatened species in Kerala.

Black body with white belly and a unique double casque.

Mostly found in the northern parts of Kerala like Wayanad and along the Kabini River belt.

These birds are not just forest dwellers – they are vital for ecological balance. Sadly, many hornbill species face threats from habitat loss and poaching.

💚 Let’s protect these beautiful messengers of the sky!
